description: A server, object store or CDN maps URL paths to existing files and sends them unchanged. No code runs per request.
The file served for a folder path: `/docs/` returns `docs/index.html`. Configured in Nginx with `index` and `try_files`.
The response header that tells the browser how to interpret the bytes. Browsers trust it over the file name.
Adding a content hash to an asset name (`app.3f9a1c.css`) so it can be cached forever: new content means a new URL.
`no-cache` stores the response but revalidates it before every use; `no-store` forbids storing it at all.
An attack that uses `..` segments (often encoded as `%2e%2e`) to read files outside the web root.
An error page served with status 200. Crawlers index it as real content; serve status 404 instead.
